html:
Simeon I, called the Great, ruled Bulgaria from 893 to 927, a time when it became the largest state in southeastern Europe and a centre of Slavic learning.

A son of Boris I, he was educated in Constantinople and was meant for the church. As ruler he moved the capital to Preslav and fought the Byzantines for decades, crushing them at Anchialos in 917 and calling himself tsar of the Bulgarians and Romans. His court fostered the Preslav school, where scholars spread the Cyrillic alphabet and translated Greek books into Old Church Slavonic, which later reached Serbia and Rus. He died in 927, before he could take Constantinople. His son made peace, and Byzantium recognised the Bulgarian ruler as tsar.
